slides.title: With only one of six conditions for exclusivity at signing even partly met, the 'don't sign yet' hypothesis stands

claims.claim: Value 1 does not hold: The $2.0M signing payment adds value on top of royalties

claims.claim: Value 2 partly holds (plan case only): Exclusivity creates value even in the low case, with realistic overlap
evidence: +$2.2–2.8M at plan; −$0.04M to +$0.55M at 65% volumes, Sales' 30–70% overlap (p. 5–7)

claims.claim: Evidence 3 does not hold: The product is production-ready in the OEM's hardware
evidence: 98.8% lab uptime against 99.5% required; no loaded or peak test; assessment not started (p. 8)

claims.claim: Evidence 4 does not hold: OEM volumes and the growth story are reliable enough to commit on
evidence: Shipments unaudited; 14,000 'booked devices' without purchase orders; competitor case correlational (p. 9)

claims.claim: Alternatives 5 does not hold: Exclusivity is the only way to win the OEM's volume
evidence: The OEM will consider N (nonexclusive, $350 a robot) and M (gated exclusivity) (p. 11–12)

claims.claim: Protection 6 does not hold: The contract protects Boreal if forecasts or certification miss
evidence: No audit right, no royalty floor after the advance, no release triggers, no code escrow (p. 10)

claims.claim: The problem is exclusivity before evidence, not exclusivity itself: the answer is a gated path, not a flat 'no'

slides.title: As drafted, the contract leaves Boreal exposed on six terms, with a scope that blocks the growing direct channel

claims.claim: Audit rights: No clear right to audit reported shipments
evidence: Risk: Royalties and volume gates rest on unaudited OEM reports
Required: Independent, shipment-level audit right; quarterly reports reconciled to invoices

claims.claim: Royalty floor: None once the $2.0M advance is used up
evidence: Risk: Direct channel barred with no minimum income
Required: Annual minimum royalty; exclusivity lapses automatically if missed

claims.claim: Release triggers: No automatic release
evidence: Risk: Locked in if the model is retired or certification slips
Required: Automatic release on model retirement, certification slip or missed minimums

claims.claim: IP protection: Source code delivered as freely reusable OEM IP
evidence: Risk: Loss of Boreal's core asset and future leverage
Required: Source code escrow with narrow release conditions; no IP transfer

claims.claim: Scope: All new North American sales, including customers on other OEMs' robots
evidence: Risk: Chief strategic opportunity cost: about $1.48M a year of direct margin at risk
Required: Limit to the OEM's robot series; carve out existing and other-OEM customers

claims.claim: Guarantee offset: Partner can demand an offset if guaranteed performance is missed
evidence: Risk: The $2.0M can claw back, e.g. if certification delays 2027 shipments
Required: Define the offset; cap it at the unearned balance; no offset for OEM-driven shortfalls

claims.claim: Existing direct contracts cannot be terminated for convenience, so any exclusivity can cover only future new North American robot sales
evidence: Without that limit, Boreal faces unquantified contract claims
